title: Two-open induction step for perfect-complex descent
statement: Let I be a directed preorder, (R_i) a directed system of Noetherian rings, c a colimit cocone, i an index and s:X_i → Spec R_i finitely presented. Let W be a quasi-compact open and V an affine open of X_i. If P(W) and P(V), then P(W ∪ V), for the explicitly fixed descent predicate [def-pc-perfect-descent-on-open]. No hypothesis of descent of objects on the intersection is needed: only descent of the overlap morphism is used.

source.place: Tag 09RF, proof: two-open gluing induction step (Tags 09RE, 079W, 08FE, 08DG)

proof.text: Fix an open-immersion presentation of W ∪ V and a perfect object E on its limit base change. Restrict E to the inverse images of W and V and apply the two descent hypotheses. Directedness puts their stage objects at a common later index. Derived pullback of local strictly perfect models preserves perfectness. Because X_i is quasi-separated and W,V are quasi-compact, W ∩ V is quasi-compact and its stage morphism is finitely presented. Apply [lem-pc-perfect-descend-morphisms] on this stage overlap to the comparison isomorphism between the restrictions of the two descended perfect objects, and increase the stage to get an isomorphism c whose pullback is the prescribed overlap identification.

Take the adjoints a,b of the two comparison isomorphisms by [lem-pc-ringed-spaces-derived-adjoint]. Use [lem-pc-restrict-derived-direct-image-open] to regard both as maps into the restrictions of the same Rf_* E. Naturality of adjunction and the equation specifying the limit pullback of c make these maps compatible on the overlap. Apply both the object and morphism clauses of [lem-sc-derived-open-gluing] on the stage union. This gives an object F restricting to the two perfect objects, and a map d:F → Rf_* E restricting to a,b.

F is perfect because this property is local on the two opens. The adjoint Lf*F → E of d restricts on each open to the given comparison isomorphism. Its cone has zero cohomology locally and hence globally, so it is an isomorphism. The open-subscheme pullback identifications identify f with the exact canonical stage-to-limit map in P(W ∪ V). Transport along the given open-immersion presentation supplies the claimed predicate. Empty W, empty V, equal opens and disjoint opens cause no extra hypotheses: all restrictions and compatibility equations exist on the empty overlap.

lean.statement:
theorem perfect_descent_open_union
    {I : Type u} [Preorder I] [IsDirected I (· ≤ ·)]
    (R : I ⥤ CommRingCat.{u}) [∀ i : I, IsNoetherianRing (R.obj i)]
    (c : Cocone R) (hc : IsColimit c) (i : I) (Xi : Scheme.{u}) (s : Xi ⟶ Spec (R.obj i))
    [LocallyOfFinitePresentation s] [QuasiCompact s] [QuasiSeparated s]
    [∀ Z : Scheme.{u},
      HasDerivedCategory.{w} (SheafOfModules.{u} (moduleRings Z.toRingedSpace))]
    [∀ (Z : Scheme.{u}) (U : Z.Opens),
      HasDerivedCategory.{w} (SheafOfModules.{u} ((moduleRings Z.toRingedSpace).over U))]
    (W V : Xi.Opens) (hW : IsCompact (W : Set Xi)) (hV : IsAffineOpen V)
    (dW : PerfectDescentOnOpen R c i Xi s W)
    (dV : PerfectDescentOnOpen R c i Xi s V) :
    PerfectDescentOnOpen R c i Xi s (W ⊔ V)
